license_summary.general: Fisher, American marten, river otter, bobcat, and mountain lion may only be harvested by North Dakota residents. Bobcat, fisher, American marten, and river otter pelts must be tagged by the Department (fishers/marten/otter: register harvest within 12 hours; bobcat Zone 1: present pelt and carcass for inspection and tagging no later than 14 days after the close of the season or before sale/transfer; bobcat Zone 2: report within 12 hours). Carcasses of fisher, American marten, river otter, and bobcat remain the property of the Department. No person, taxidermist, or fur dealer may possess or purchase untagged animals of these species. All trapping and cable device seasons and raccoon/beaver hunting open at one-half hour before sunrise (Central Time). Written permission is required to trap or use a cable device on private land.

species.notes: Beaver and raccoon may be taken at any hour of the day, while hunting on foot, with the aid of artificial light, night vision, thermal vision, or infrared light with a power source of not more than 6 volts (light must produce a red, green, or amber color, except when taking a raccoon treed or at bay). Beaver dams may be partially or completely dismantled when their presence causes property damage.

species.notes: Bobcat may only be harvested by North Dakota residents. Zone 1 is land west of US Highway 83 from the Canadian border to the South Dakota border; Zone 2 is the remainder of the state. Pelt tags are available from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service for pelts of captive born and raised lynx in North Dakota (F2 generation or later) with documented proof.
permit_requirements: Zone 1: the pelt and carcass of each bobcat must be presented to Department personnel for inspection and tagging no later than 14 days after the close of the season (March 29, 2027), or prior to sale or transfer of possession, whichever comes first. The pelt must be removed from the carcass before presentation; the carcass remains Department property.
Zone 2: report the harvest to the local game warden or Department field office, or register online via your account, within 12 hours and make arrangements to have the bobcat tagged.
No person, taxidermist, or fur dealer shall possess or purchase an untagged bobcat.

species.notes: Mountain lion is included in the small game/furbearer proclamation but is managed as a big-game-style hunt: residents only, HUNTING ONLY — the use of traps or cable devices (snares) to take mountain lions is prohibited. Zone 1 is south of ND Highway 1804 from the Montana border to Lake Sakakawea, across the lake, then south along ND Highway 8 to ND Highway 200, west on 200 to US Highway 85, south on 85 to the South Dakota border; Zone 2 is the remainder of the state. Kittens (visible spots) and females accompanied by kittens may not be harvested.
permit_requirements: Harvesters must contact the local game warden or Department field office, or register online via their account, within 12 hours and make arrangements to have the mountain lion tagged.
The entire mountain lion, including the head, must be presented for inspection and tagging. Legally taken animals are returned to the hunter for pelt removal; the carcass remains Department property.
Harvest quotas close seasons immediately; the Department announces closures through press releases, PSAs, and media contacts.

species.notes: 2026 is the first year fisher can be harvested statewide (previously restricted to the Turtle Mountains). Hunting of fishers is prohibited — traps or cable devices only.
permit_requirements: Fishers may only be harvested by North Dakota residents.
Trappers must contact the local game warden or Department field office, or register their harvest online via their account, within 12 hours and make arrangements to have the fisher tagged.

The fisher pelt must be removed from the carcass before presenting to Department personnel; no pelt is tagged until the animal is skinned and presented with the entire carcass, including the head. The carcass remains Department property.
No person, taxidermist, or fur dealer shall possess or purchase an untagged fisher.

verification.confirmation_notes: Data taken from the official 2026-2027 Small Game, Waterfowl and Furbearer Proclamation text published on gf.nd.gov (retrieved 2026-09-18). Sections 19 (beaver/raccoon), 20 (weasel/mink/muskrat), 21 (bobcat zones), 22 (red fox/gray fox/coyote/badger), 23 (mountain lions), 24 (fisher and American marten — first-ever marten season, statewide fisher), 25 (river otter, new 3-week season Nov 23-Dec 13 with no quota), and 27 (protected furbearers with official Latin names). Calendar-check: Nov 7, 2026 is a Saturday; Nov 23, 2026 is a Monday; Nov 29, 2026 is a Sunday; Dec 13, 2026 is a Sunday; Mar 15, 2027 is a Monday; Mar 29, 2027 is a Monday. Southwestern North Dakota observes Mountain Time; the proclamation prescribes hunting hours in Central Time.
known_gaps: Year-round species (beaver, raccoon, red fox, gray fox, coyote, badger) are modeled as season_status 'continuous' with continuous_open true and null dates, per the Iowa schema convention; the proclamation's Apr 1–Mar 31 license-year framing is recorded in the season notes.
Scientific names (other than the five protected species in Sec. 27) are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in the proclamation.

Striped skunk: the 2026-27 proclamation contains no provisions for skunks, so no skunk season was modeled — verify against North Dakota Century Code whether striped skunk may be taken and under what authority.
Weasel: the proclamation says 'Weasel' without specifying species; modeled as 'Weasel' with no scientific name.

Mountain lion is included in the furbearer proclamation as a hunting-only, residents-only managed hunt (traps/cable devices prohibited) with zone quotas; its Zone 1 early/late/conditional structure is as published.
Zone boundaries are summarized; the illustrated zone maps (Figure 2 bobcat, Figure 3 mountain lion) should be consulted for exact boundaries.
Nuisance/depredation take (e.g., beaver damaging property, livestock defense) is mentioned in passing but not modeled.
Fort Berthold (Three Affiliated Tribes) furbearer rules are a separate jurisdiction and are not reflected in this state dataset.

Southwestern North Dakota (south and west of the Missouri River — e.g., Adams, Bowman, Golden Valley, Hettinger, Slope counties) observes Mountain Time; the dataset uses America/Chicago statewide. The proclamation states hunting hours in Central Time — adjust for Mountain-Time counties.
